description: Plan step L6 (design step S4 second half; graph node schedules). loops.peak-start and loops.peak-end: what happens when a peak begins and ends, per the ten-row decision table of design sec 6.9 item 4, reading the rules board's service; M7's execute.resume-drive is called only when the contributed action list contains it (it does not exist yet). Also the workspace-registry listing of projects. Probe required. Depends on FEAT-012.
steps: Read loops design sec 6.9 completely (items 1-4, the ten-row table of item 4, F40/F48 notes), sec 6.1 (listing projects from the workspace registry, cold start V17), sec 5.2 (loops.peak-start executed by the rules board, loops.peak-end executed here), sec 17 M7 item 6 (resume-drive contract: done/skipped/failed within 60 s). Read src/shared/peak-mode.ts (stateFor, stateForProject, peakHoldFor; the loop board only reads them) and src/shared/pricing.ts.

Specs first (new tests/loops-peak.spec.ts; extend tests/fake-rc3.ts: execution-row Contribution with execute.resume-drive configurable to done / skipped / failed / throw / no answer within 60 s; goals.get; peak mode service stateFor/stateForProject): one case per row of the ten-row table (row 3 with done, skipped, failed, throw, timeout and with the contribution not containing the action; both reduce and stop levels; holder session cold and hot; cold session is restored through resolveAgent only when the main-step record says it walked in this peak or cannot be read; after skipped the goal is read and an active goal is recorded as done; inform level does not restore a cold session; row 5 is the same path for reduce and stop (main agent exempt); row 2 stores 'judge again' and after hand-over the process that takes over judges, so run happens at most once across both; row 9 reason codes and resolveAgent first for a cold session; main-step.json written by another process and unreadable cases; walking back by minute to find the peak start); the level shown on the page and in view.json comes from stateForProject(projectRoot) and shows 'check the level on the rules board' when it returns undefined or the service is absent; a goal blocked with hourness-idle-rounds is never touched; the project list comes from the workspace registry (list() may throw when it is not started: degrade, retry on the next beat).

Implement src/loops/peak.ts, project listing in src/loops/index.ts (or a small projects.ts if the file grows), the peak-start entry execution handoff (self, by rules: the loop board only lists and records it, the rules row does the work), view.json fields for peak/level text. Wrapped host calls; never throws.

Probe: extend scenario loops with the shifted clock: peak end with no resume-drive in the execution contribution -> the main agent is reminded once when it was idle and worked in this peak; no double reminder after a restart. Record results in findings.
Docs: ORCHESTRATION.md loop board section (peak end), DESIGN.md. Commit once or twice; messages carry gate results including the probe exit code.
acceptance_criteria: All ten rows of the item-4 table, in both levels where the table says so, have a passing test; the main agent is reminded at most once per peak end.
With M7 absent (no execute.resume-drive in any contribution) the loop board never calls it and still reminds the main agent where row 3 would have and the table says so.
The loop board reads only stateFor / stateForProject / peakHoldFor and never the rules board's files.
build, preflight, npm test and npm run probe exit 0 (or only the recorded baseline failures); row still disabled in the patch.
verification: npm test (TEMP = system temp directory) exits 0
findings:
Implemented 2026-11-01/02 by resuming the interrupted run feat-013-peak-edges (Kiro credits ran out mid-run; its uncommitted prep was kept and finished).
Implementation: src/loops/peak.ts (the ten-row end-of-peak table, rows in order; row 3 calls execute.resume-drive only when a hand-over lists it, revives a cold session first when the walk record says it worked this peak, 60 s limit, idempotent-skipped falls through per review F40); peak-start is recorded and delegated (level of the moment, self entry, never run here); project listing and view.json peak line from stateForProject; fake-rc3 gained the execution-row contribution, goals.get and the peak-mode service.
Tests: tests/loops-peak.spec.ts, one case per row (row 3 with done/skipped/failed/throw/timeout/absent action; both levels on rows 5+10; row 2 held and rerun with the same run, expiry; cold vs hot sessions; main-step unreadable and written-by-another-process; minute-walk back to the peak start; duplicate end edge across a restart).
Two concurrency defects fixed on top of the inherited work, found because the suite was flaky (about one failure in two runs across four tests): (1) run.ts now serializes its beats through one promise chain — the file watch fires beats without waiting, and two concurrent beats read the same journal bytes; (2) inbox.ts save() no longer replaces the state object (in-place prune) and saves run one at a time through a write chain, so a run or a delivery in flight can no longer lose a held judgement, an armed run, or the inbox position to a stale snapshot landing last.
Probe: the scenario check compared the numeric step clock with LOOPS_PEAK_END as a STRING constant — a number compared with a string coerces the string to NaN and the check could never pass; LOOPS_PEAK_END_MS (Date.parse) added for the comparison, the string stays for the event key. probe 198/198 (was 197/198).
Gates on this tree, serial: npm run build exit 0; npm run preflight exit 0 (eslint 249 suppressed, knip 21, jscpd 2); npm test exit 0 (1564/1564, loops-peak.spec.ts added to the list); npm run probe exit 0 (198/198). Both loop rows stay disabled: true.
